title: The Town Where the Lights Go Out at 9

scenes.note: The harbour town at night, every window lit… then at "nine o'clock" every light goes out at once
Not one streetlight (a lamp clicks off over a kid)
Not one TV (a family window goes dark)
Total darkness: only the lighthouse beam sweeps over the roofs
Kids walk home in the dark, counting under their breath
Most kids count the big ones: 300 to the bakery…
…600 to school
Leo: "But I count everything."
Stairs. Fence posts. Cracks in the sidewalk. Out loud. (numbers pop as he walks)
At school they laugh: "CALCULATOR!"
Only one light stays on after nine: the lighthouse on the rocks
Grandpa at the lighthouse door: forty years
But Grandpa's eyes are getting worse
He holds the rail with both hands
Every evening I climb with him
Looking up the spiral: 214 steps
I've counted them a thousand times
Up top, Grandpa shows him the old oil lamp
"If the generator ever dies… this keeps the boats safe."
When I counted, Grandpa just smiled
"Lighthouse keepers count too."
The night of the big storm
Dad's fishing boat still out in the waves
He's always home before nine. Mum and Leo wait at the window
At nine o'clock the town went black
The lighthouse flickered… and went out
The generator was dead
Dad's boat heading straight for the rocks in the dark
Grandpa grabs his coat but can't even find the door
"Leo… I can't do the stairs."
So I went.
612 steps from our door to the lighthouse, counting in the rain
Running up the stone path to the dark lighthouse
Inside: so dark he can't see his own hands
But I didn't need to see (hand finds the rail)
Seventy-one, the cracked step
One hundred and fifty, the turn
Two hundred and fourteen: the top
The matches: third shelf, left side
The first match blew out. So did the second.
The third one caught
The old lamp roars to life, the giant lens blazes
…and threw its light across the sea
Far out, the tiny boat turns away from the rocks
Just in time
Dad's boat reaches the harbour at 10:52
I know, because I counted every minute
The whole town waiting on the dock in the dark, lanterns up
Grandpa hugged me like he'd never let go
Now on stormy nights nobody laughs at the kid who counts
They count with me (the whole town on the seafront, the beam passing over)
